subject.title: fix(acp): handle Gateway replace deltas in translator, not byte-offset slices

question: When Gateway emits `replace: true`, should OpenClaw buffer until an authoritative snapshot is stable or deliberately begin a new ACP message identity?
rationale: ACP provides streamed chunks and message boundaries but no retract operation; buffering changes latency, while a new identity can expose both the superseded and revised messages to users.

options.title: Buffer revised output
options.body: Coalesce replacement-prone snapshots and emit one authoritative ACP message without exposing stale content.

options.title: Begin a new message
options.body: Give the revision a new message identity, accepting that clients may visibly retain the superseded message.

recommendation.title: Buffer revised output
recommendation.body: Coalesce replacement-prone snapshots and emit one authoritative ACP message without exposing stale content.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACP translator, lifecycle, and hardening history makes this the strongest available owner for the bridge's user-visible protocol semantics.
